problem: The closed form alpha r_1^n + beta r_2^n needs r_1, r_2 to be distinct roots of r^2 = pr + q; for a double root the general solution is (alpha + beta n) r^n.
corrected: a_{n+2} = pa_{n+1} + qa_n,\ r_1 \ne r_2 \text{ roots of } r^2 = pr + q \Rightarrow a_n = \alpha r_1^n + \beta r_2^n

problem: Beatty's theorem needs alpha, beta > 0 (e.g. alpha = -sqrt2 gives 0 < beta < 1 and the statement fails), and the sets should be indexed by n >= 1; braces are otherwise ambiguous with the fractional-part notation.
With unsigned lengths PA*PB = |PO^2 - r^2| (negative right side for P inside); the equality without absolute value holds only for signed lengths. The cyclic criterion requires ABCD convex.
